flora: Kelp Blade Cross-section (thick, honeycombed internal cellular air structure that gives it buoyancy)
Conceptacle Concept (microscopic reproductive pits on the fertile frond surface releasing motile biflagellate zoospores)
Young Kelp Sporophyte (slender, small rubbery blade beginning to split, anchored by a tiny button-shaped holdfast)
Holdfast Detail (root-like, highly textured, thick solid disc firmly gripping a dark grey glaucconitic rock surface)
environment_details.style_notes: STYLE_ANIMATED_FEATURE_V3; emphasis on distinct tactile textures—from slick, wet, rubbery outer cuticles to the porous, dry interior cells; optimized for educational quadrant identification.

visual_logic.composition: A clean quadrant-tiled layout separating four analytical biological components: Top-Left: Close-up of a cut blade showcasing its internal cellular honeycomb buoyancy structure; Top-Right: Macro view of the textured frond surface showing reproductive conceptacle pores releasing tiny spore dots; Bottom-Left: A single, tiny young sporophyte showing early growth development; Bottom-Right: A high-detail view of the solid, bulbous holdfast anchoring system.
visual_logic.ground: A clean, wet marine-studio surface composed of a smooth dark grey-green rock background to provide high contrast for the golden-brown structures.
visual_logic.lighting: Clear, bright, even diffused daylight with minimal harsh shadows, carefully balanced to capture the wet, glossy, high-contrast sheen of the marine plant tissue.
